codeReview.summary: The evaluator SubprocessTransport was correctly refactored to use the engine registry for command building, mirroring the dispatcher's pattern. The implementation adds engineName and evaluatorModel parameters, resolves engines from the registry, checks binary availability with Bun.which(), builds commands via engine.buildDispatcherCommand(), uses engine-specific output parsing (NDJSON for OpenCode, plain text for Claude), and preserves the 30s timeout and retry-once behavior. The evaluator maintains its own system prompt separate from the dispatcher. 24 new tests were added covering both engine routes, default models, config overrides, error handling, output parsing, schema validation, backward compatibility, and env filtering. All 2928 tests pass with clean typecheck.

issues.description: extractTextFromNDJSON is duplicated verbatim between dispatcher/subprocess-transport.ts (line 37) and evaluator/subprocess-transport.ts (line 42). This is a DRY violation — the function could be extracted to a shared utility (e.g., src/utils/ndjson.ts or src/worker/ndjson-parser.ts which already handles NDJSON). Not blocking because both copies are identical and tested, but increases maintenance risk if the NDJSON format changes.

EVALUATOR_SYSTEM_PROMPT is a minimal one-line string ('You are an evaluator checking whether worker output meets the validation criteria. Evaluate the output against all provided criteria and respond with valid JSON only.'). While functional, this same text also appears as the first line of buildPrompt() (line 159), meaning the evaluator instruction is partially duplicated between the system prompt and the user message. The Claude route sends both --system-prompt and -p, so the model sees this instruction twice. Not a bug (redundancy is harmless for correctness), but slightly wasteful on tokens.

The stdinContent construction for the OpenCode route concatenates EVALUATOR_SYSTEM_PROMPT + separator + userMessage + retryNote. However, buildDispatcherCommand() was already called with the prompt and systemPrompt in the options — the systemPrompt content is effectively ignored by OpenCode's buildDispatcherCommand() (which only uses model). This means OpenCode's stdin prompt construction is correct but slightly confusing architecturally: the system prompt is manually prepended to stdin rather than being handled by the engine command builder. The dispatcher has the exact same pattern, so this is consistent.

sharedStateObservations.observation: extractTextFromNDJSON helper function is now copy-pasted across two transport files (dispatcher and evaluator). As more transports adopt this pattern, AGENTS.md or the architecture library should document that NDJSON parsing utilities should be shared, or the function should be extracted to a shared module to prevent further duplication.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/dispatcher/subprocess-transport.ts:37 and src/evaluator/subprocess-transport.ts:42 contain identical extractTextFromNDJSON implementations (15 lines each)

sharedStateObservations.observation: The evaluator transport is not yet wired into the main execution pipeline. The Evaluator class in invoke.ts receives its transport via DI, but no production code currently instantiates SubprocessEvaluatorTransport with engine parameters — the evaluator is only used in tests. AGENTS.md mentions this is expected (infrastructure-first approach), but the feature description says 'wire evaluator model configuration' which implies it should be connected. The wiring gap may need a follow-up feature.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: grep for 'SubprocessEvaluatorTransport' in src/controller/ returns no results. Only test files instantiate it. The execution-loop.ts has a maxEvalCycles config but no evaluator transport construction.

summary: PASS. The evaluator transport refactoring correctly mirrors the dispatcher's engine-aware pattern. Implementation is clean, well-structured, and follows established conventions. All 24 new tests are meaningful and cover the expectedBehavior items. Three non-blocking issues identified: (1) extractTextFromNDJSON duplication between dispatcher and evaluator transports, (2) minor token-wasteful duplication of evaluator instructions in both system prompt and user message for Claude route, (3) architectural inconsistency in how system prompts are handled for OpenCode stdin (manually prepended rather than through engine command builder). No blocking issues. Backward compatibility is preserved via default engineName='opencode'. The worker followed the skill procedure faithfully (TDD red→green, full test suite, typecheck).
